questions.q: A price change moves average order values far from the training distribution, while the churn relationship itself is unchanged. What is this?
options: Concept drift
Data drift
Label leakage
Overfitting
questions.explain: Data drift means the input distribution changed. Concept drift means the input-to-outcome relationship changed.

questions.q: In the lesson's simulation, week 3 had normal-looking inputs but AUC fell to 0.544. What does that show?
options: Input drift checks are enough to protect a model
The endpoint was misconfigured
PSI thresholds should be set to zero
Concept drift can hide from input monitoring, so quality must be tracked with delayed labels too
questions.explain: When customers' behavior changes without input distributions changing, only ground-truth-based quality metrics reveal the problem.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the Model Monitor workflow described in the AWS docs?
options: Schedule, baseline, capture, violations
Baseline, violations, capture, schedule
Violations, schedule, baseline, capture
Data capture, baseline, schedule, review violations
questions.explain: Enable data capture, create a baseline from training data, schedule monitoring jobs, then read the violations report.

questions.q: What does the AWS documentation say about SageMaker Model Monitor's availability, as of this lesson's writing?
options: It is no longer open to new customers; existing customers can keep using it
It was deleted for all customers
It is only available in one region
It is free for all customers
questions.explain: The docs note it is closed to new customers and point to open-source SageMaker monitoring samples with Evidently AI, QuickSight and CloudWatch. Always check the current documentation.

questions.q: The lesson flagged features when PSI exceeded 0.25. Where does that threshold come from?
options: It is the default Model Monitor threshold
A common rule of thumb chosen for the exercise, which you should tune for your own data
It is required by the SageMaker API
It is derived automatically from the model's AUC
questions.explain: 0.25 is a widely used rule of thumb and a choice in this lesson, not an AWS default. Thresholds should be tuned to your data and cost of false alarms.
